Cavs and Hawks tussle twice in three daysThe fourth-seeded Cleveland Cavaliers host the fifth-seeded Atlanta Hawks in a game that carries genuine postseason weight and a potential first-round playoff preview. Both teams arrive in Cleveland with legitimate playoff seeding implications as Cleveland has an outside chance of slipping into the third seed, while Atlanta looks to hold off a slew of teams in the rearview at the fifth seed. With a second meeting already scheduled for Friday, April 10 in Atlanta, Wednesday’s tip-off is the opening act of a two-game series that could shape how both franchises enter the postseason. Where Both Teams StandCavsCleveland enters at 50-29, second in the Central Division and one game behind the New York Knicks, who own the tiebreaker, while Atlanta comes in at 45-34, leading the Southeast Division by two games over the Orlando Magic. Despite a shaky 14th-ranked defense, the Cavaliers have been one of the league’s hotter teams of late, going 8-2 over their last 10 games — a stretch that includes road wins at Utah and Golden State, a home victory over Indiana, and a wild 142-126 road win at Memphis on April 6. Cleveland’s offense ranks fourth in the NBA at 119.6 points per game, powered by a trio of stars. Donovan Mitchell leads the team at 27.8 points per game on 48.1% shooting, while reigning Defensive Player of the Year Evan Mobley contributes a versatile 18.2 points, 8.9 rebounds, and 3.7 assists per game on 54.8% from the field. Midseason acquisition – and 11-time All-Star – James Harden has been a seamless fit, averaging 23.7 points, 8.1 assists, and 4.9 rebounds while shooting 43.7% from the field and 37.5% from beyond the arc. Center Jarrett Allen adds 15.3 points and 8.5 rebounds per game on a consistent 64.2% shooting, which is fifth in the NBA. Hawks Atlanta has been equally impressive, going 7-3 over its last 10 games and 18-2 in its previous 20 before their narrow 108-105 home loss to the Knicks on April 6. The Hawks rank sixth in the NBA in scoring at 118.4 points per game, led by Jalen Johnson’s surging all-around production of 22.7 points, 10.3 rebounds, and 8.0 assists per game. Nickeil Alexander-Walker has been a revelation alongside him, averaging 20.8 points per game on 45.7% shooting and 39.9% from three, with five 32-point performances this season. Onyeka Okongwu is averaging 15.3 points, 7.7 rebounds and 3.2 assists while shooting 47.9% from the field. Dyson Daniels rounds out the core with 11.8 points, 6.8 rebounds, and 5.8 assists per game, while leading the team with 1.9 steals per game and shooting a team-best 51.7% from the field.Watch Cavs vs. Hawks on FuboTV for free Matchup to watch: Cavs’ defense against Jaylen Johnson The central chess match on the floor will be Jaylon Johnson against Cleveland’s frontcourt. Johnson, who has recorded 48 double-doubles this season, is a rare blend of size, skill, and playmaking that creates problems for any defense. Mobley — one of the more versatile defensive bigs in the league — figures to draw the primary assignment, but Johnson’s ability to handle, pass, and score from multiple levels makes him difficult to contain with a single defender. On the other end, Atlanta’s rebounding vulnerability is a legitimate opening for Cleveland to exploit. The Hawks are being outrebounded by 1.8 per game on the season, and with Landale out, their interior depth is thin. Mobley at 8.9 rebounds per game and Allen at 8.5 give the Cavaliers a frontcourt capable of winning the glass decisively. Injury Cloud Hangs Over ClevelandThe biggest question mark heading into tip-off is the availability of Mitchell, who is listed as questionable with a right ankle sprain after sitting out the April 6 win in Memphis. If Mitchell cannot go, the offensive burden shifts squarely to Harden and Mobley — both capable of carrying a heavy load, but Mitchell’s absence would fundamentally alter Cleveland’s attack and remove its most dynamic scoring threat from a matchup where Atlanta’s backcourt, led by Alexander-Walker, has been on a tear. Dean Wade (ankle) and Jaylon Tyson (toe) are both questionable, while Thomas Bryant (calf) has been ruled out. For Atlanta, the primary concern is center Jock Landale, who is out for at least two weeks with a right high-ankle sprain sustained April 1 against Orlando — an injury that is likely to keep him sidelined for the remainder of the regular season. The Hawks have signed Tony Bradley to a rest-of-season contract to provide frontcourt depth, but Onyeka Okongwu will be asked to anchor the interior with Mouhamed Gueye and Bradley behind him.Watch Cavs vs. Hawks for free on DIRECTV What are the latest odds for Cavs vs. Hawks?
